In [[algebra]], a '''noncommutative Jordan algebra''' is an [[algebra over a field|algebra]], usually over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] of [[characteristic of a field|characteristic]] not 2, such that the four operations of left and right multiplication by ''x'' and ''x''<sup>2</sup> all commute with each other. Examples include [[associative algebra]]s and [[Jordan algebra]]s.

Over fields of characteristic not 2, noncommutative Jordan algebras are the same as [[flexible algebra|flexible]] Jordan-admissible algebras,<ref>{{harvnb|Okubo|1995|pp=19,84}}</ref> where a '''Jordan-admissible algebra''' – introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Albert|year=1948}} and named after [[Pascual Jordan]] – is a (possibly [[non-associative algebra|non-associative]]) algebra that becomes a Jordan algebra under the product ''a''&thinsp;∘&thinsp;''b''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''ab''&nbsp;+&nbsp;''ba''.
